title: BSTabDiff: Block-Subunit Diffusion Priors for High-Dimensional Tabular Data Generation
claim: Latent block variables from a structured prior are decoded through parallel copula and marginal modules, then reordered, to produce realistic high-dimensional data.
layout: Single panel, top-to-bottom flow with branching blocks, arrows and equations in boxes
description: A single-panel architecture flowchart. At top left, a gray 'Label Prior p(Y)' box feeds a large light-blue box 'Latent Block Variables' holding blue ovals h1, h2, ..., hM, labeled 'Diffusion / Flow Model'. An arrow leads right to a dashed peach box 'Missingness Mask', which shows a binary vector R = 1 0 1 1 0. Three arrows fan out from the latent box to Block 1, Block 2 and Block M. Each is a rounded box with the equation Z_j = a_j h_t + b_j(Y) + ε_j above an inverse-CDF line. A gray bar below them reads 'Gaussian Copula & Marginal Decoding'. Arrows run down to an 'Observed Feature Permutation π' step. A teal 'Canonical Space' binary table joins it from the left. The mask arrow and the permutation arrow both end at 'Permuted Output', a table of X1...XM labeled 'Observed Space'. The eye lands on the blue latent box first.
caption: Architecture of BSTabDiff. The model samples a label, then draws low-dimensional block-latents h1, . . . , hM using a learned diffusion/flow prior. Each block governs a subset of features via copula-Gaussian decoding and inverse marginal CDFs to yield realistic marginals. A missingness mask is generated in parallel. The output is then restored to the original feature order, yielding high-dimensional tabular data with structured dependence, marginals, and missingness.
abstract: High-Dimensional Low-Sample Size (HDLSS) tabular domains (e.g., omics) are characterized by $n \ll m$, where $n$ = number of samples, and $m$ = number of features. Such domains often exhibit strong local correlation groups, sparse cross-group dependencies, heavy-tailed non-Gaussian marginals, heteroscedastic noise, and structured missingness, making direct density learning in $\mathbb{R}^m$ ill-conditioned since $n \ll m$. We propose BSTabDiff, a block-subunit generative framework that partitions the $m$ observed features into $M$ latent blocks ($M \ll m$) and generates each block via a shared low-dimensional subunit variable, concentrating global dependence learning in the compact block-latent space $\mathbb{R}^M$ while decoding to the full feature space with copula-driven dependence, flexible per-feature marginals, and explicit missingness mechanisms. BSTabDiff can induce a data-driven feature ordering and block construction before latent partitioning, allowing the model to better align with local dependency structure when such organization is beneficial. BSTabDiff supports modern deep priors on block latents, including diffusion and normalizing flows, enabling stable synthesis and controllable benchmark generation in the HDLSS regime. Empirically, BSTabDiff produces more realistic and more stable high-dimensional synthetic data when compared with unstructured tabular generators on HDLSS data.
